permit.exempt_list_quote: City (FAQ): "Permits are required for all work except minor repairs and decorating. Minor repairs to structures may be made without a permit, but such repairs shall not include the cutting away of any wall, partition or portion thereof, the removal or cutting of any structural beam or bearing support, or the removal or change of any required means of egress, or rearrangement of parts of a structure affecting the exit requirements; nor shall minor repairs include addition to, alteration of, replacement or relocation of any standpipe, waste supply, sewer, drainage, drain leader, gas, soil, waste, vent or similar piping, electric wiring or mechanical equipment or other work affecting public health or general safety." State (Ohio Building Code): "102.10 Work exempt from approval. Approval is not required for the following work; however, this work is still to comply with all applicable provisions of the rules of the board: Building: 1. One-story detached accessory structures used as tool and storage sheds, playhouses and similar uses, provided the floor area does not exceed one hundred twenty square feet (11.15 m2) and playground structures. 2. Fences not over seven feet (1829 mm) high. 3. Retaining walls which are not over four feet (1219 mm) in height [...] 4. Water tanks supported directly upon grade [...] 5. Sidewalks, parking lots and driveways not more than thirty inches (762 mm) above grade [...] 6. Finishes not regulated by this code, decorating, or other work defined as maintenance or minor repair. 7. Temporary motion picture, television and theater stage sets and scenery. 8. Window awnings supported by an exterior wall of Group R-3. [items 9 to 18: temporary structures, tanks, signs and others] [...] 102.10.2 Minor repairs. Minor repairs to structures may be made without application or notice to the building official. Such repairs are not to include the cutting away of any wall, partition or portion thereof [...]"
permit.note: Neither the city's wording nor the state list names toilet partitions or compartments ('partition' in the minor-repairs sentence means a wall). The city's permit guide lists 'Alterations' and 'Building Repair' among work that needs a permit, and its only list of work that needs none is for 1-, 2- and 3-family dwellings. The contractor registration page refers to 'Maintenance work as described in Cincinnati Building Code 1101.17'; that section (Municode) could not be opened. The state pack shows the code regulates toilet partitions as interior finish (HDPE fire test), so 'finishes not regulated by this code' doesn't settle it.
permit.second_quote: Permits are required for the following: New buildings; Additions (bedrooms, bathrooms, family rooms, etc.); Alterations (decks, garages, fences*, carports, awnings, haunted houses,interior demolition etc.); Building Repair; Demolition (structure); Change of Occupancy and Use; Excavation or Fill; Developments in a floodplain [...] Separate permits are required for: [...] Plumbing work, plumbing fixtures, or plumbing appliances (such as dishwashers) [...] When Don't I Need A Permit? Generally, you don't need a permit for these projects at 1-, 2- and 3-family detached dwellings*: [...]

restrooms_city.rule: Cincinnati Municipal Code Chapter 886, Equitable Restrooms (Ordinance 348-2021, passed 2021-09-01, in force from 2022-01-01): every single-occupancy restroom in a public building or place of public accommodation must be available to all persons and carry exterior signage that identifies it as a restroom and does not limit it to a specific gender. Applies to existing and future buildings. A violation is a Class C1 civil offense.
restrooms_city.quote: Sec. 886-01. - Definitions. [...] (b) "Single-occupancy restroom" means a fully enclosed room, with a locking mechanism controlled by the user, containing no more than one sink, one toilet, and one urinal. Sec. 886-03. - Single-occupancy Restrooms. (a) All single-occupancy restrooms located within a public building or place of public accommodation, including family restrooms and accessible restrooms, shall be made available for use by all persons, regardless of their sex, gender identity, physical or mental capacity, or familial status. (b) All single-occupancy restrooms located within a public building or place of public accommodation shall be outfitted with exterior signage that identifies the single-occupancy restroom as a restroom and does not indicate use of the restroom is limited to a specific gender. (c) This provisions of this chapter apply to all existing and future public buildings and places of public accommodation operating on or after the effective date of this chapter. Sec. 886-05. - Penalties and Enforcement. (a) A violation of any provision of this chapter shall constitute a class C1 civil offense. [...] Section 5. That this ordinance shall take effect and be in force from and after January 1, 2022.
restrooms_city.note: Read as the scanned ordinance attached to the City Council's legislative record (file 202102521, enactment 0348-2021, status Passed, passed 2021-09-01). The codified Chapter 886 on Municode could not be opened, so later amendments or a repeal are not ruled out. 'Place of public accommodation' is defined by reference to Section 914-1-P1, not read. No city rule on shared all-gender rooms was found.

page.meta: Commercial bathroom partitions delivered to Cincinnati job sites. Price your restroom, choose a material and see the Ohio and city rules that apply.
page.lead: Commercial bathroom partitions for Cincinnati offices, schools, hospitals and university buildings, shipped by freight to your job site.
page.stall_bullet: - **How many stalls:** Ohio's statewide building rules set the number of toilets and urinals by how many people use the building, and Cincinnati enforces them. The table below shows what that means.
page.restroom_bullet: - **Single-user and all-gender restrooms:** a one-person restroom must be marked as open to everyone. Cincinnati has its own rule as well: in public buildings and places open to the public, every one-person restroom must be available to all and carry a sign that doesn't limit it to one gender, and this covers existing buildings too. A shared all-gender room is allowed outside schools and colleges if every toilet sits in its own compartment with a door, the compartments meet a set privacy rating, and urinals are in stalls or screened from view. Since February 2025, Ohio law requires shared student restrooms in schools and colleges to be designated for one sex; one-toilet family restrooms are still allowed there.
page.permit_bullet: - **Permits:** Cincinnati requires a permit for alterations and building repairs, and says permits are needed for all work except minor repairs and decorating. Neither the city nor Ohio's list of exempt work names toilet partitions. Ask the Cincinnati Department of Buildings & Inspections whether your replacement needs one. You don't need a permit to buy partitions.
page.confirm_office: the Cincinnati Department of Buildings & Inspections
page.install_rule: Cincinnati requires every contractor working inside the city limits to hold a current city contractor registration, renewed every year, and the city doesn't issue a building permit until the contractors on the job are registered. Ohio licenses only five commercial trades at state level: electrical, HVAC, hydronics, plumbing and refrigeration. Partition installation isn't one of them. You don't need a permit to buy partitions.
page.faq_install_extra: A contractor working in Cincinnati needs a current city contractor registration.
page.public_jobs_bullet: - **Public jobs:** on state, county and city projects over $250,000 for new construction or $75,000 for remodeling, Ohio law requires at least the wage the state sets for each trade in each county; school district projects are exempt from that law. The state publishes its Hamilton County rates on a portal that needs a login. On federally funded building work in Hamilton County, the federal rate for a carpenter is $32.26 an hour plus $19.10 in benefits.
page.sales_tax_bullet: - **Sales tax:** 7.8% in Cincinnati: 5.75% state, 1.25% Hamilton County and 0.8% transit authority.
page.buyers_extra: - **Hospitals and medical offices:** stainless steel, phenolic or HDPE that stands up to frequent disinfecting, with accessible stalls in every room.

Sales tax: the Department's October 2026 table gives 7.80% for Hamilton County. The date that rate began (reported as October 1, 2020) wasn't read on an official page, and the Department's rates for January 1, 2027 weren't found: recheck in January.
The Ohio Board of Building Standards has proposed code amendments (Group 107, revised September 2026) with no effective date; they don't touch the toilet counts. Recheck when adopted.
Nearby cities Covington, Florence and Independence are in Kentucky: the Ohio rules, tax and wage figures on this page don't apply there.
